newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Mobutu said to be leaving Switzerland for France.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu said to be leaving Switzerland for France.

text.p: Swiss authorities have decided not to renew the visa of ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko of Zaire, currently undergoing treatment for cancer, when it runs out on October 27, Swiss television reported on Friday.
It said the 66-year-old ruler would probably be moving to a luxury villa he owns at Cap Martin near Nice in the south of France.

Mobutu, who came to power with the support of the United States and other Western countries in 1965 after a long period of unrest in the vast, mineral-rich state, now has few friends in the outside world.

He is widely regarded as having presided over an increasinly corrupt administration. United Nations investigators and non-governmental organisations assert there have been widespread abuses of human rights under his rule.

The Swiss government granted a "humanitarian visa" in August to allow him to come to the country to undergo an operation for prostate cancer at the University Hospital in Lausanne, 60 kms (37 miles) east of Geneva.
After the operation on August 22, he and a large suite of aides have been living in the city's luxury Beau Rivage on the shores of Lake Geneva -- one of the most expensive in Switzerland.

The Swiss television report said the government in Berne had decided not to extend the visa "to avoid further controversy". Left-of-centre political figures and human rights groups have been strongly critical of the decision to allow him in.
There was no immediate comment from Swiss officials on the report, and hotel staff and aides to Mobutu decline any discussion of his health.
According to the report staff at Mobutu's "Villa del Mar" at Cap Martin have been preparing for his arrival there for the past few days.
It said Zairean Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo, who visits the president regularly in Lausanne to discuss government affairs, had persuaded the French authorities to allow him to transfer there.
The report said doctors treating Mobutu with chemotherapy in Lausanne believed he needed to continue the treatment until the end of the year, but would be able to follow the treatment in France.

According to Swiss TV Mobutu, widely believed to have transferred large sums of money abroad during his long rule, had some $4 billion in banks in Switzerland -- about half of a reputed total of $8-10 billion in accounts around the world.
